source: In our data set, 15% of film writers were women; 85% were men.
why: The files hold per-word rates only (word-level counts and rates for female- and male-written scripts; wall.csv for all scripts). None of them records writers or scripts, so a share of writers by gender cannot be computed from these tables.

source: In April 2016, we broke down film dialogue by gender. The essay presented an imbalance in which men delivered more lines than women across 2,000 screenplays.
why: This finding comes from the authors' earlier dialogue study, not from this screen-direction data: the methodology here states that dialogue was excluded from the analysis, and the three files contain only word counts/rates for screen-direction bigrams beginning with "he" or "she".
